title: JoinString clones a single-element join that already aliases a tracked value, doubling the root charge
claim: strings.Join of one element with a non-empty separator returns the element itself; JoinString's alias fast path only handles separator=="", so joinStringHit clones and adopts a second root with identical ranges, spending up to 64 KiB of extra allocation and root charge per call.

title: Repository fuzzing covers only a narrow slice of the exact/coarse transition space
claim: FuzzEngineSequence covers 6 operation kinds with 2-element joins and 1-byte replace (32 or fewer matches); the >16-element join, >32-match replace, empty-old, ValidUTF8, Case/Coarse and multi-window paths are fuzzed only by the review harness, not in the repository.

title: The >16-element join gate inspects 16 elements, but the coarse fallback reads only 15
claim: For joins with more than 16 elements, the MayContain gate covers elements[0..15] but the coarse fallback reads elements[0..14] plus the separator; taint only in element 15 wastes a slow path and yields no provenance, within the documented bounded-prefix trade-off.

title: RepeatBytes looks up the store before its cheap bounds check
claim: RepeatBytes performs MayContain and Lookup (a snapshot copy) before checking withinByteBounds, so results that can never be adopted still pay the lookup.
